title: Prometheus
subtitle: Prometheus carries the numbers that decide whether GPUs earn their keep, follows a fleet that changes under it, and pages one operator's phone.

lede: In Inference Fabric generic service health told me nothing about whether the GPUs were earning their keep, so I instrumented the quantities that decide GPU economics: padding, cache reuse and token conservation. The broker exports its own metrics into a Grafana dashboard, and GPU utilisation comes from NVIDIA's DCGM exporter beside the runtime's counters. The token-accounting panel is how I proved the broker fix in Millions of queued items that were not there. Each step of From 44K to 163K tokens per second is a capture from these dashboards.
quote: A panel that should read zero is a test; any non-zero difference between tokens received and routed is a defect.
evidence: Observability and alerting: Prometheus, Grafana and alerting built end to end, about 137 broker metrics on a 31-panel dashboard and 12 scrape jobs across hosts, GPUs and inference nodes.
GPU utilisation monitoring: token-conservation and padding panels beside DCGM exporter data, with 96.9% SM utilisation on the larger card in the 163,000-tokens-a-second run.
Dynamic service discovery: provisioning code writes GPU nodes into Prometheus's file-based service discovery as agents add and drain them, so monitoring follows the fleet.
author: Corey James
